Utility pane

Five utility panes

Source, Filesystem provenance, Suggestion runs, Error log and Tab history, in one file because they share one problem: they are the views nobody opens on purpose, so they kept the original stylesheet while everything else moved. Each tab keeps its own state, so you can leave a source draft pending, start a collection, switch away and come back to both.

Source

A gutter and a text area, with the three states the document cares about: a clean pane, a pending draft, and a draft that has been outranked by a change from another view. Edit the text and the state line moves to pending; use the menu to simulate another view changing the ontology and it becomes stale, where Apply is withdrawn and the only way forward is Discard draft and reload, exactly as written: "the draft is retained and cannot overwrite that newer version." Nothing is discarded by closing the pane.

The format list implements the published table including its gate: this document contains a named graph, so Turtle, RDF/XML and N-Triples are disabled with the reason, because they cannot retain it. That is a structural impossibility, so the option withdraws rather than failing after you pick it.

Filesystem provenance

Folder, options, progress, evidence, in that order, with the four counts the panel already reported. Collect runs for a few seconds so the progress, the current path and Cancel are all real. A cancelled collection is kept and labelled partial rather than thrown away, and the primary action becomes Open partial provenance ontology, which is what the shipped panel does. Coverage notes are counted separately from errors because they are not failures.

Suggestion runs

Sequential, which is the whole character of this view: one target at a time, a failure that does not stop the queue, and a target list frozen at the moment the batch was invoked. Change the selection in Hierarchy all you like; this list does not retarget. A failed run keeps a reference to its own error log entry, and the Error details action on that row switches to the Error log tab and opens that entry, which is the handoff the two documents describe but the app spells as two unrelated panels.

Error log

Operation, time, failing stage and a timeline, then the diagnostic sections collapsed until opened: prompt, assistant response, stdout, stderr, exit code, executable and arguments. The published limits are enforced here rather than mentioned: stderr keeps its last 8,000 characters and a diagnostic field keeps at most 262,144 and says when it truncated. Credentials are redacted before display, so the bearer token in the sample prompt is already gone. A cancelled request is a separate kind of entry, not a failure. One entry is a log write failure, which still shows its record and says it could not be saved.

Tab history

Grouped by type, then by creation date in YYYY-MM-DD, with a filter that searches names, types and dates together, because the document says it searches all three and a filter that silently only matches names is worse than no filter. The retention setting is in the action row, and switching it to Named tabs only greys the default named entries rather than deleting them, since changing the setting preserves what is already saved.

What is seeded rather than live

The source document, the provenance walk, the run queue, the error records and the saved tabs are all fixtures. The timing, the counts, the truncation, the gating of formats and the cross tab handoff from a failed run to its log entry are real.
